The 4-hour live order timeout enforces again, and the root cause is fixed at every call site that cancels.

CAUSE: Kalshi sharded its matching engine. READ endpoints aggregate across shards; WRITE endpoints do not. Every cancel went out unrouted, so a cancel for an order resting on a non-default shard was answered 404 not_found permanently. One order sat 3.5 days past its timeout, alive at queue rank 1 in the same second a cancel was refused.

FIXED ACROSS: #368 recorded the diagnosis; #370 put the error class and body into the log MESSAGE so the cause was readable at all (it had gone to a structured field the log service drops); #377 routed the timeout cancel by the market's own exchange_index, which Kalshi documents as authoritative; #380 extended that to the drain and queue-aware cancels and added timed_out_cancel_failed to the cycle summary.

VALIDATED IN PRODUCTION, not in a fixture: the specific order that opened this ticket cancelled on the first reconcile cycle after #377 deployed (15:08Z), and the post-#380 soak at 17:54Z was clean — 0 stuck past timeout, 0 cancel failures, 0 drain_unconfirmed and 0 rejections in 24h.

TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, recorded rather than quietly dropped:
1. OWNER DECISION OPEN — three KXBTCD rows from 2026-09-06/07 carry cancel_reason drain_unconfirmed from before the routing existed. Given what is now proven they were almost certainly alive and merely unroutable, so that terminal reason describes something that did not happen. NOT corrected: rewriting terminal history is an operator's call, not an agent's.
2. Placement routing was DISCARDED, not deferred. Kalshi's 2026-08-27 change auto-routes orders carrying a market ticker; user_not_found rejections went 41/44/13 on 08-28/29/30 and zero every day since. XOS-000014 needs no code from us and should be re-read against this before anyone builds for it.

RESIDUAL: the drain and queue routing are inferred from the proven timeout path, not independently observed — they make the byte-identical call, and the drain only runs for stood-down books.

Also settled: Kalshi's cancel endpoint DOES honour exchange_index. Secondary sources claimed only index 0 was supported; that is wrong. Their documentation is unreachable from the build environment, so this was established empirically against the live reproduction."}},{"command_id":"lo-tc-link-380","action":"ADD_LINK","actor":"claude-code","actor_role":"LIVE_OPS","schema_version":1,"payload":{"issue":"XOS-000028","link_type":"PR","reference":"380","label":"Routes the drain and queue-aware cancels; adds the refused-cancel counter."}}]
